record.tranche_reason: The post reports experiments about superposition in ResNet-18 models, but does not test the claim versions about neuron-pole job shares, cross-model scaling, canonical polysemantic examples, architecture/tool effects on interpretability, neuron-based attribution graphs, or explanation quality.
record.gate_note: The post reports its own measurements of feature-cluster separation and similarity under baseline versus active-learning training. These results concern superposition proxies, not the claimed share of interpretable neuron poles or the other specified versions. Cited results and descriptions from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The post compares baseline and least-confidence active-learning training of ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet. It uses class-cluster proxies (t-SNE, cosine similarity, silhouette, Davies-Bouldin) and a few activation-maximization images that it calls superposition. It measures no share of interpretable or monosemantic neurons and runs no neuron audit, explanation scoring or attribution graphs. It does not test whether architecture or tools raise that share. Its results do not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The author concludes that active learning performed worse on both datasets and seems to have more superposition. Suggested causes are uninformative sample selection or overfitting to uncertain samples. Further work should try other sampling strategies, deeper models and better-quality data.
record.recipe_differences: This is an active-learning training comparison on ResNet-18 vision models, using feature-space proxies; it does not reproduce the neuron-pole audit or explanation-testing methods in the claim's original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The post reports different outcomes across CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet; the active-learning comparison uses least-confidence sampling.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, active-learning ResNet-18 showed higher mean feature cosine similarity (0.927 vs 0.885) and lower silhouette (0.189 vs 0.212) than baseline. Davies-Bouldin was nearly equal (1.542 vs 1.551), t-SNE showed more overlap, and activation-maximization images were judged noisier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, least-confidence active-learning training yields less separated class clusters in feature space, which the author reads as more superposition.

fits_no_version.finding: On Tiny ImageNet, active learning gave lower mean cosine similarity (0.254 vs 0.310) and lower silhouette (-0.399 vs -0.348) than baseline. Its Davies-Bouldin index was described as higher, t-SNE showed more overlap, and activation-maximization images were judged more crowded.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In ResNet-18 on Tiny ImageNet, least-confidence active-learning training yields poorer class-cluster separation, which the author reads as more superposition.

record.peer_reviewed: LessWrong post; peer-review status not stated
record.problems: The post says CIFAR-10 images make neuron features difficult to interpret; activation maximization covers only a few randomly selected units, and the units across models are not directly comparable. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The post itself notes that its active-learning model did not outperform baseline overall and suggests that data selection or overfitting to uncertain samples may have hindered generalization.

untested.parts: The Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit shares (about 90% one job, 7% two related jobs, 2–4% not yet understood).
Job shares in other language models, dense or mixture-of-experts, at any scale.
Reinterpretation of canonical polysemantic neurons such as InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron. The post only recounts the Circuits car/dog example as superposition.
The interpretable-neuron share as a function of architecture, regularization or tools. Training data selection is varied, but no interpretable share is measured.
Neuron-based attribution graphs versus replacement models.
Explanations from activating examples versus held-out activation prediction.
Simulation-based automated scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The superposition proxies are class-level feature-space cluster metrics, not per-neuron monosemanticity measures. The activation-maximization comparisons cover four random units, and the author concedes units across models are not directly comparable. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The post is not an original source and gives no verdict on any version.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B audit and its proportions of one-job, two-job, and not-yet-understood neuron poles.
Neuron-pole job shares across language models, dense and mixture-of-experts models, or model scales.
Whether InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron detects a coherent shared feature or exemplifies recursive generalization rather than superposition.
Whether architecture, regularization, tools, or model capacity determine the share of interpretable neurons; no interpretable-neuron share is measured.
Attribution graphs, neuron-based circuit units, replacement models, and reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict neuron activations on unseen examples.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.
